false_belief: I have to react or get even when things feel unfair.
true_belief: I can pause, respond honestly, and choose calm actions even when something feels unfair.

false_belief: Everything has to happen right now, or waiting ruins the fun.
true_belief: I can handle waiting and disappointment, and anticipation can make good things sweeter.

false_belief: If people say no, leave, or forget, it means they don't care about me.
true_belief: I can trust the people who love me even through mistakes, distance, or disagreement.

false_belief: Someone else's success or praise means I am less important.
true_belief: I can celebrate others while my own worth and journey stay intact.

false_belief: If I can't do it quickly or easily, I'm not smart or capable.
true_belief: Everyone learns and improves at their own pace through practice.

false_belief: Plans and things must happen exactly the way I expect.
true_belief: I can adapt when plans change and still find or create joy.

false_belief: One mistake means I'm not capable, not good, or a bad person/friend.
true_belief: Mistakes are part of learning and growing, and I can take responsibility and keep going.

false_belief: I can't cope or be okay when my body or surroundings feel uncomfortable.
true_belief: I can care for myself, ask for help, and know uncomfortable moments will pass.

false_belief: Being blamed for something means nobody believes me.
true_belief: I can respond honestly and calmly even when something feels unfair.

false_belief: I should always get to decide, choose, or go first.
true_belief: I can cooperate and take turns even when I don't get my way.

false_belief: One setback, loss, or failure ruins everything and can't be undone.
true_belief: I can rebuild, recover, and begin again after setbacks.

false_belief: Feeling afraid means I should stop or avoid the unfamiliar thing entirely.
true_belief: Courage is taking one small brave step even while afraid.

false_belief: Loud, sudden, or unknown things mean I'm not safe.
true_belief: I can find safety, calm, and support even when things feel uncertain.

false_belief: If I feel nervous, I can't do the thing or I'll be remembered forever for messing up.
true_belief: Confidence grows each time I try, and courage means continuing despite nerves.

false_belief: My results, score, or performance decide whether I'm good enough.
true_belief: My effort and learning matter more than any single result.

false_belief: If something hurts, I can't handle it.
true_belief: I am stronger than I think, even during difficult moments.

false_belief: New or unfamiliar people won't understand, help, or accept me.
true_belief: Trust grows one step at a time, with new people too.

false_belief: When something good ends or is lost, it's ruined or gone forever.
true_belief: Endings bring new beginnings, and people help rebuild after hard things.

false_belief: My small actions don't make a difference, so there's no point.
true_belief: Small caring actions can genuinely help create a better future.

false_belief: Being left out, ignored, or unfollowed means I don't matter or nobody likes me.
true_belief: One moment of being left out doesn't decide my worth or my friendships.

false_belief: I won't fit in or be accepted in this new place.
true_belief: I can make genuine connections while being myself, even somewhere new.

false_belief: Love disappears or life will never feel happy again when someone is gone.
true_belief: Love stays with us through memories, and life can hold joy again.

false_belief: I can't be okay without this special object.
true_belief: The comfort I feel lives inside me too, not only in the object.

false_belief: Growing up or changing means losing who I used to be.
true_belief: Growing changes me, but I'm still me inside.

false_belief: Distance or less time together means love becomes smaller.
true_belief: Love stays strong even when people are far away or busy.

false_belief: If a friend leaves, moves, or spends time elsewhere, the friendship is over.
true_belief: Real friendships can continue and grow across distance and change.

false_belief: A big change means everything familiar is gone or ruined forever.
true_belief: Home and stability are built through love and can grow again after change.

false_belief: My appearance, size, or looks decide my value or lovability.
true_belief: My worth comes from who I am, not how I look.

false_belief: Having more things, nicer things, or others' experiences would make me happier.
true_belief: Gratitude for what I have brings more lasting joy than comparison.

false_belief: I have to be like someone else to be valued or accepted.
true_belief: My unique strengths and identity make me valuable as I am.

false_belief: Not being chosen or favored means I'm not good enough or less important.
true_belief: My worth isn't decided by awards, roles, or someone else's favor.

false_belief: Talent is something you either have or don't have.
true_belief: Practice helps me improve my own abilities over time.

false_belief: Someone new getting attention means I've been replaced.
true_belief: Love grows to include new people; it isn't divided up.

false_belief: If another family's rules are different or looser, my parents are being unfair.
true_belief: Every family makes choices based on its own needs and reasons.

false_belief: I have to follow every exciting feeling or urge right away.
true_belief: I can enjoy excitement and still guide my attention and calm my body.

false_belief: Being tired means I have no control over my behavior.
true_belief: I can notice my feelings and still choose kind actions, even tired.

false_belief: I should always keep going and do everything perfectly without rest.
true_belief: Rest is part of learning and growing, and I can do my best while caring for my energy.

false_belief: Waiting is pointless, unbearable, or ruins the fun.
true_belief: I can use waiting time calmly and wisely, and anticipation can be sweet.

false_belief: I have to be good, perfect, or no trouble at all to be loved.
true_belief: I am loved even while I'm learning, growing, and making mistakes.

false_belief: If I have to wait to share something, what I want to say isn't important.
true_belief: My thoughts matter, and I can wait for the right moment to share them.

false_belief: Hiding the truth or a mistake will protect me.
true_belief: Honesty brings trust, even after mistakes, and hiding just adds weight.

false_belief: I must follow the group, break rules, or hide who I am to belong.
true_belief: Doing what's right and honoring my identity matters more than fitting in.

false_belief: The world or a situation is only unfair, and bad behavior always wins.
true_belief: Fairness grows through understanding, courage, and responsible action.

false_belief: Rules only matter when they're convenient, or cheating is fine if it helps me succeed.
true_belief: I can choose integrity regardless of what others do, and honest effort matters more.

false_belief: Keeping every secret, even an unsafe one, makes me a good friend.
true_belief: Safe adults should know secrets that could protect someone.

false_belief: Everyone I meet online or elsewhere can automatically be trusted.
true_belief: I protect myself by making safe choices and asking trusted adults.

false_belief: Someone else's struggle, fear, or need isn't my place to help with.
true_belief: Kindness and small encouragement can make a real difference for someone else.

false_belief: I have to prove myself to everyone, especially against rumors.
true_belief: Truth and character matter more than what others say about me.

false_belief: Holding on to hurt keeps me safe from being hurt again.
true_belief: Forgiveness helps relationships heal and grow, in my own time.

false_belief: I have to choose one friend over another.
true_belief: I can be kind and fair to everyone without ranking who I care about.

false_belief: I have to control others for things to go well.
true_belief: Cooperation grows through patience and honest communication.

false_belief: Including more people, younger or new, will spoil the fun or take up needed room.
true_belief: Everyone deserves a chance to belong, and including others can add to the fun.

false_belief: The loudest or most insistent person should be heard first.
true_belief: Listening is an important way to show respect for everyone.

false_belief: If people don't understand me, something is wrong with me.
true_belief: I can express myself patiently and still be myself.

false_belief: I can't stay calm when I feel physically trapped or confined.
true_belief: I can find peaceful ways to handle uncomfortable, confined moments.

false_belief: I have to believe every scary thought that crosses my mind.
true_belief: Thoughts are not always facts, and I can return to the present moment.

false_belief: If I fall or fail once at something physical, I shouldn't try again.
true_belief: Trying again helps me grow stronger and more confident.

false_belief: Someone or something else's pain has nothing to do with me.
true_belief: Caring actions can comfort others and genuinely make a difference.

false_belief: If I forget a name or make a small social slip, people won't like me.
true_belief: Everyone makes small mistakes, and kindness repairs them.

false_belief: Being picked last or called clumsy means I'm not good enough to belong.
true_belief: Skills improve with practice and effort, and belonging isn't earned by skill.

false_belief: A mistake made publicly, in front of others, makes me less worthy.
true_belief: One embarrassing moment doesn't change my worth.

false_belief: Fair means I should get an identical turn or outcome every single time.
true_belief: Fairness includes patience and considering everyone's needs, not identical outcomes.

false_belief: I can't feel safe anywhere except home.
true_belief: I can feel safe in new places when I'm with trusted people.

false_belief: If I found something, it automatically belongs to me.
true_belief: Doing the right thing matters more than keeping something unclaimed.

false_belief: If someone copies my work or idea, I've lost what made me special.
true_belief: My ideas and creativity remain valuable even if others draw from them.

false_belief: Someone else will notice and help the person who's alone or struggling, so I don't need to.
true_belief: Small acts of kindness from me can make someone feel welcome.
